meta.source: Nathan 2026-10-14: use ZSTD (Zstandard) — the compression layer for the system's data

zstd_layer.law: ZSTD (Zstandard) is the Archive's compression layer. Everything the system keeps gets squeezed; the 15 MiB budget holds more.
zstd_layer.what_it_is: Meta's LZ77 + FSE/Huffman compression: fast decompression, high ratio, dictionary support, streaming. Verdict on the pasted explainer: the technical claims are right (kernel/Cloudflare/K8s usage, dictionary compression, configurable levels); the hype is hype.

plugs_in.archive_holdings: holdings compressed under the 15 MiB rate-distortion ceiling — compression multiplies the budget
plugs_in.project_ingest: dictionary compression trained on the 449-HTML corpus — the files share massive boilerplate (three.js, scaffolds), dictionaries turn that redundancy into near-free storage
plugs_in.event_log: world-state snapshots + signal/event history compressed for replayable runs
plugs_in.best_parts: compression happens AFTER best-parts extraction — squeeze what's kept, don't keep what's squeezable-noise
plugs_in.cloudflare_workers: Worker response payloads + world-state sync compressed at the edge — ZSTD is already Cloudflare's native path, so this is swimming downstream

zstd_layer.not_for: not a replacement for rate-distortion triage (what to keep is still the Archive's decision); not for the hot neural path (decompression cost stays off the tick)
zstd_layer.queue: Archive compression pass once the indexer ingestion is underway.
zstd_layer.verdict_second_explainer: Same accurate core (mechanism, levels, streaming, usage). The '10x faster/smaller with dictionaries' claim is inflated marketing — dictionaries help most on small structured records, not universally. 'Gold standard' is framing, not fact. No new adoption beyond the Workers payload note.
